text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- King Hussein meets Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Jordan's Red Sea port of Aqaba; Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawnah delivers a letter from the monarch to Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak.

- A Jordanian-Israeli accord reached in principle to solve the water row over an extra 50 million cubic metres to Jordan in two stages; under the accord part of the water is to be supplied immediately and the remaining by three years.
- The Islamic Action Front (IAF) opposition party keeps its options open on boycott of the next parliamentary elections due in November.
- King Hussein and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu discuss how to activate the peace treaty and reviving the stalled Middle East peace process.
- Ten opposition parties and nationalist figures decide to fight coming elections on one platform; a general congress to crystallise a programme of "national salvation."
- Islamic Action Front leadership decides to coordinate with the other leftist opposition parties ahead of coming elections.
- Tarawnah discusses in Cairo with Egyptian officials bilateral ties and Middle East peace developments.

- Jordan concludes an initial accord with Israel which ensures its water rights under its 1994 peace treaty with the Jewish state; the arrangement supplies the kingdom with an extra 50 million cubic metres of drinking water.
- Royal decree issued appointing Samir Zeid Rifae as head of Crown Prince Hassan's special office.
